name: new-project-cwd-needs-domain-mapping
tags: cwd_domains.json new project domain mapping tasks memory epic scaffold workflow checklist
body:
Whenever a brand-new project directory is created (e.g. scaffolding a new repo for an epic, `mkdir` + `git init`), add an entry to cwd_domains.json right away — don't wait for it to come up as a problem later.

Location: `~/Library/Mobile Documents/com~apple~CloudDocs/Databases/cwd_domains.json` (iCloud-synced, path resolved via claude-hooks-dev's `src/config.py::Config.cwd_domains_json`). Format: flat `{"<directory-name>": "<domain>"}` map — usually the same string for both (e.g. `"cypress-playwright-migrator": "cypress-playwright-migrator"`).

Why: `src/tools/tasks.py::_domain_from_cwd` resolves a task's domain by walking the cwd's path components in reverse and matching against this map by EXACT component name (not substring, not full path) — see config.py's `_load_cwd_domain_map`/`cwd_domain_map`. A new project directory with no entry here means tasks__create/list calls with `cwd=<new project path>` silently fail to resolve a domain tag, which can affect task filtering/organization down the line even though task creation itself doesn't hard-fail on a missing mapping.

How to apply: as soon as a new project cwd is created (mkdir + git init, or scaffolding a sibling repo for an epic), immediately add `"<dirname>": "<domain>"` to cwd_domains.json in the same step — treat it as part of "creating the project," not a separate followup. This was done for `cypress-playwright-migrator` (epic fd7c8e12) on 2026-07-15 right after creating the directory.
